svg.text: FIGURE 12
The Bond: How Composition Carries Meaning
Why a list of ingredients is not a molecule, and what the arrangement costs.
Figures 5 and 6 say when a composition is worth having and where it may reach. Neither says what a composition is.
A set of ingredients is not one. The bond is the rest of the information, and it is the half nothing was recording.

Two words this figure introduces, used by every claim below it
A bond is the typed relation between two operands. There are seven, they are not interchangeable, and which one holds is not recoverable from the operands. A
recipe that names only its ingredients has recorded half of itself.
A molecule is a bonded arrangement. A chain is the degenerate case: one bond type, no branching. Nothing about a chain is a different kind of object.
The seven bonds, and whether the order of the operands matters. Negation is the eighth operator and is not a bond; see the amendment below.

Six tests, and they separate the seven bonds. Seven is a count of bonds, not of operators. Whether there are additional bonds is a question no test derived from these can answer. A relation that fails all
six is not a bond you are missing. It is a claim that has not been made yet.
Symmetry is what decides whether an arrangement is a new thing. Under a symmetric bond, k operands have k! spellings and one term, so a code that charges
for the sequence overcharges by log₂(k!) while the bond term undercharges. Both wrong, in opposite directions, and only one is usually noticed.
The arrangement is the substance.
Two entries with an identical ingredient set are not variants of one thing. They are different things whose notation cannot tell them apart, and the difference is
carried entirely by the bond. Two entries can share every ingredient and be inverses of one another.
This is not an analogy. Chemistry hit it first: silver fulminate and silver cyanate have the same composition and different properties, which is what forced
structure into the notation. Liebig and Wöhler, 1824 to 1826; named isomerism by Berzelius, 1830.
A bond costs what it could have been, and nothing more.
The price of an arrangement is the choice it records, so it is logarithmic in the number of bonds available. With one bond type the term is zero, and it rises
as the vocabulary of bonds grows, and only then. A bond that costs nothing is a bond that carries nothing, which is the flat case.
Which is the same bargain as the term itself, one level in: Rissanen’s minimum description length applied to the relation rather than to the operands.
Composition is recursive, and the level decides what is irreducible.
A settled molecule becomes an atom for whatever composes over it. So irreducible is a fact about a level and never about the world, and there is no bottom
for the same reason Figure 4 says there is no top: the transform between levels is lossy, and the level a composition lands on remakes it.
Which is why a system that cannot settle has one level however large its library. Nothing composes over what was never admitted as a part.
Settling compresses the description and not what it cost to establish. Whether that cost must be paid again depends on the substrate: where the arrangement is
recorded, re-deriving it is a lookup and the actions were spent once. Where it is not, the result carries forward and the deriving does not, so every lineage pays
again. Which boundary matters is the one the record does not cross. Inside a run the arrangement persists and nothing is re-earned; across a boundary that drops it,
everything is.
A vocabulary without bonds can name a state and cannot name a route to one.
A plan is a sequence. A goal is a comparison. Progress is a subtraction. A refutation is a negation, and that one is not a bond. A system holding only ingredients can say what a
situation contains and cannot say what would count as getting somewhere from it.
Which is the bound that would bite at the middle of Figure 3’s chain. Whether it is what breaks there is not yet measured, because a link below a break cannot be
read. What can be said is that having terms for what a situation affords was taken for a dictionary and it is a grammar.
Four structures a compositional system exhibits, and each names something the flat form cannot write.
isomer. Same atoms, different bond, different substance. The difference is invisible in the formula and decisive in the behaviour.
catalyst. A part that survives its own use. Spent and regenerating parts behave differently across uses, and nothing records which a term is.
cycle. The output re-enters as input. The sign of the loop decides whether it closes, and a chain cannot close by construction.
functional group. A substructure whose presence fixes the outcome. The group says what kind; the qualifier says which member.
A composition costs in two currencies, and they do not add.
Bits price the description. Actions price finding out whether it holds. They are in different units, so a system holding one accounting cannot compare them
and will not notice the shortfall. It proposes arrangements it cannot afford to test, and the budget is what decides how much of the space is reached at all.
The two readings come apart in both directions. A long chain of cheap parts is expensive to describe and may cost one action to refute. A short arrangement
over a costly operand is cheap to state and may take a whole budget to settle. Neither figure predicts the other, so both are read or the choice is made blind.
Summing them into one figure is the error this names, not the fix for it. A price in bits and a price in actions are two readings, held apart.
How to read the claims here. The two collapses are failures of notation and follow from what the notation records. The pricing rule follows from minimum description length.
The recursion and route claims are structural: they say what a compositional system requires, not what any one of them exhibits.

Figure 5 says when a composition is worth having. Figure 6 says where it may reach. Figure 12 says what it is, and what the arrangement costs, so Figure 8’s surplus can be a bond the other frame holds and you do not.
AMENDMENT · a bond is a binary operator, and this figure defines the bonds. It does not define the unary ones.
The seven are bonds, and a bond is a relation between two things. Negation is not one: it takes a term and yields a term, and joins nothing. So it is not an eighth bond,
and it is not a relation that fails the six tests. It is a unary operator, outside what the tests range over, which is a different verdict from the one above and reached differently.
Which matters for the rule this figure states. A relation failing all six is a claim that has not been made yet — and that rule is about relations, so it still holds for every
candidate that joins two operands, including a composition whose parts cancel. Cancellation is a property a molecule turns out to have, not a way of attaching terms.
So the operators divide by arity, and this figure describes the binary ones. Without a unary operator a system can write what a situation contains, what follows what, and how far
along it is — and it cannot write that any of those is false. A vocabulary that cannot refuse can only accumulate. See the Operators table for the entry and its open price.
How to read this. It is an addition, not a correction: the seven are correctly characterised as bonds, and the claim is that bonds are not the whole of the operator set.
